summary.headline: Q1 FY27 operating income rose 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore, EBITDA margin 10.5%, while order inflow nearly tripled to Rs 8,519 crore.
summary.overview: Revenue grew 6% YoY to Rs 2,721 crore and EBITDA rose 9% to Rs 285 crore, with margin up to 10.5% from 10.1%. PAT rose 3% to Rs 141 crore. Management said Q1 revenue was held back by Vadhvan port execution not starting, and by four newly won jobs (Munger, Pune Metro, Delhi Metro, Morsagar; about Rs 10,000-12,000 crore) that had not yet begun production. Management maintained FY27 revenue growth guidance of 25%, with the bulk of catch-up expected from Q3. A Rs 5,000 crore QIP enabling resolution was approved, but management said the timing and amount depend on future orders and market conditions.

financial_highlights.change: vs about Rs 2,900 crore in Q1 FY26 (about 3x)

financial_highlights.value: about 120 days (inventory about 30 days, WIP about 107 days)

segments.name: Marine
segments.commentary: About Rs 15,000 crore of marine jobs in the tender pipeline, including Vadhvan port (execution not started), overseas jobs in Oman and UAE, and Bangladesh work. Tuticorin Outer Harbour and Vizag port also mentioned.

segments.name: Data centre
segments.commentary: Five Navi Mumbai projects (three of 140 MW, one of 130 MW and two of 30 MW) are under way; a Vizag civil job has also been secured. Total work is about 320-400 MW, with electromechanical work possibly later.

segments.name: Bangladesh transmission project
segments.commentary: Execution is under control. Completion is now guided for September/October 2026 (earlier June 2026 timing was cited by an analyst). Receivables are about Rs 178 crore plus retention.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guidance maintained at 25% (management also said 20-25% growth is achievable for a few years).
FY27 order inflow target of about Rs 25,000 crore; Rs 8,519 crore secured in Q1 and about Rs 1,247 crore added in July, with L1 positions of about Rs 900-1,000 crore.
Q3 and Q4 expected to be much better than Q1; Q2 seen as weak because of monsoon. Management cited last year's Q1 of Rs 2,500 crore, Q2 Rs 2,100 crore and Q4 Rs 3,000 crore as the pattern.
FY27 capex guided at Rs 350-400 crore, barring exceptional plant purchases such as TBMs for large road tunnels.
Working capital expected to stay at 110-120 days; gross debt expected to rise about 10-20% and at least 20-25% if top line grows 25%.

Rs 5,000 crore QIP is an enabling resolution. Management said part is for capex (Rs 4,000-5,000 crore range cited for capex needs) and part for working capital and possibly inorganic growth, with timing dependent on orders and markets.
capex_capacity: Q1 capex additions were Rs 81 crore; FY27 capex guided at Rs 350-400 crore.
Large diameter road tunnel jobs would need tunnel boring machines, raising capex well above the normal run-rate.
Management said plant older than five years is not permitted on many projects, which raises replacement capex needs.
Data centre capacity is about 320-400 MW in progress; Navi Mumbai civil works already in place.
Management said current operating capacity allows about Rs 5,000 crore of quarterly revenue, which the analyst asked about and management confirmed.
demand_pricing: Work-in-hand is about Rs 31,000 crore versus Rs 18,000-20,000 crore earlier; about Rs 12,000 crore of it had no progress yet (Munger, DMRC, Pune Metro, Morsagar).

Adani group makes up about 50% of the order book (Rs 6,000 crore of Q1 orders from the group and Rs 2,500 crore from outside). Group work is competitively bid with no fixed price, and some material is supplied free by the client.

Bid pipeline is about Rs 90,000 crore, with a hit ratio of about 15% (earlier about 20%). Six segments each carry about Rs 15,000-20,000 crore: marine, underground metro, airports, data centre, highways and bridges, and water.
Export share of order book is about 2-3%.
Management expects margin to hold in double digits, with contingency built into estimates for geopolitical and commodity risk. A government agency cut performance guarantees from 10% to 5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise Rs 5,000 crore via QIP when the company is net-cash and the order book is already Rs 31,000 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the money is for growth, with part for plant and equipment, part for inorganic growth, and part for working capital. It also said timing depends on market conditions and near-term visibility, and that little of it would be used this year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected revenue trajectory and why is growth lagging order book growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited Vadhvan (zero production so far), about Rs 10,000-12,000 crore of newly won jobs that need 6-7 months of design and mobilisation, and Abu Dhabi work that has only just picked up. It guided for 25% FY27 growth, with Q3 and Q4 stronger.

qa_highlights.question: What is Vadhvan port execution status?
qa_highlights.answer: Execution has not started. Management said pending issues are outside its control, with no timeline set; it hopes work will resume soon.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the Bangladesh project timeline moved and what is its status?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said execution remains on plan for September/October 2026. Monsoon-driven river conditions and deep-water foundation work are the constraints, and a different technology is being used. Receivables are about Rs 178 crore plus retention.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 20-25% growth sustainable, and what capex does it need?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 20-25% growth is possible over coming years. Normal segments (marine, road, industrial, airport) need about Rs 300-400 crore capex a year, but a Rs 10,000 crore road tunnel would need much more.

qa_highlights.question: What is the marine and overall competitive landscape?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are about three major marine players, with about five including others. Competition is intense and price-driven, and the hit ratio is about 15%.

risks_watch: Vadhvan port execution has not started and management says the pending issues are outside its control with no timeline; a large share of expected revenue depends on it.

About Rs 10,000-12,000 crore of newly won jobs (Munger, Pune Metro, Delhi Metro, Morsagar) need 6-7 months of design and mobilisation; their revenue contribution from Q3 is the main test of the 25% FY27 guidance.

Q2 is expected to be weak due to monsoon, and Bangladesh transmission completion has slipped to September/October 2026 from an earlier June 2026 timing, with river and deep-water foundation constraints.
Rs 5,000 crore QIP is only an enabling resolution with timing tied to orders and markets; watch how much is actually raised and deployed into plant, inorganic growth and working capital.
Hit ratio has fallen to about 15% from about 20% as bidding volume rises; about 50% of the order book and pipeline is from the Adani group, and labour shortages were acknowledged.
key_quotes: Vadhvan port execution is yet to start. There are a lot of issues has to be sorted out, which is beyond our purview, beyond our scope.
Yes, you are right. Absolutely right.
So, out of Rs. 30,000 crores, around Rs. 12,000 crores order which is available with us, where there is no progress so far because of the initial mobilization is going on.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on order inflow, the 25% FY27 revenue guidance and margins in double digits, but was evasive on Vadhvan timing, the QIP's size and deployment, and the detailed inorganic plan, saying these depend on factors outside its control or are not yet finalised.

growth.why: Management held FY27 revenue growth guidance at 25% and order inflow is ~3x YoY (Rs 8,519 cr vs ~Rs 2,900 cr), with work-in-hand at ~Rs 31,000 cr, but Q1 revenue grew only 6% and the guidance depends on a steep H2 catch-up; the Rs 5,000 cr QIP is only an enabling resolution.
